tile.name: Actual Budget
tile.tagline: Private, zero-based budgeting.
tile.description: A snappy, local-first budgeting app. Your finances never leave your cluster.
tile.postInstall: Open it and create your budget file — everything stays local.

tile.name: ADS-B Feeder
tile.tagline: See the planes flying over your house.
tile.description: Decode ADS-B with a cheap SDR and watch a live map + 24h heatmap. Feeds the community aggregators and FlightAware.
tile.postInstall: Plug in your RTL-SDR + 1090MHz antenna, then open the map. Antenna placement drives your range.

tile.name: AIS-catcher
tile.tagline: Track ships in real time on a live map.
tile.description: Decode marine AIS with an SDR and see cargo ships and ferries on a built-in map. Best near navigable water.
tile.postInstall: Plug in your RTL-SDR + VHF antenna near the coast, then open the map.

tile.name: Media Automation (*arr)
tile.tagline: Sonarr + Radarr + Prowlarr + qBittorrent.
tile.description: The classic 'media appears by magic' bundle that feeds Jellyfin. Ships with an indexer-config and VPN story.
tile.postInstall: Configure your indexers in Prowlarr and connect qBittorrent — set up a VPN before you do.

tile.name: Audiobookshelf
tile.tagline: Your audiobooks and podcasts, with great phone apps.
tile.description: A self-hosted server for your audiobook and podcast library, with progress sync across excellent iOS and Android apps. Point it at a folder and go.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your admin account, then add an audiobook or podcast library folder.

tile.name: FreshRSS
tile.tagline: A fast, self-hosted RSS reader.
tile.description: Follow the web on your terms. Lightweight, quick, and great with mobile clients.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your account, and add a few feeds to get started.

tile.name: Home Assistant
tile.tagline: Automate your home — the #1 self-hosted app.
tile.description: The open-source home automation hub. Beloved, powerful, and a genuine weekend project rather than a five-minute setup.
tile.postInstall: Open it and follow the onboarding wizard to create your account and add your first devices.

tile.name: Immich
tile.tagline: Google Photos at home — searchable and private.
tile.description: A self-hosted photo and video library with face recognition, semantic search, and phone auto-backup. The consensus #1 show-your-friends app.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your admin account, install the mobile app, and turn on auto-backup. Runs its ML best on the x86 node.

tile.name: Jellyfin
tile.tagline: Your own Netflix — no accounts, no paywall.
tile.description: Stream your movies, shows, and music from your own hardware. Hardware transcoding runs best on the x86 node's Quick Sync; keep transcoding off the Pi.
tile.postInstall: Open it to run the setup wizard: create your admin user and add a media library folder.

tile.name: Karakeep
tile.tagline: Bookmark everything, with AI tagging.
tile.description: A self-hosted 'bookmark everything' app with optional AI tagging. Pairs with the Ollama tile or an API key.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your account; AI tagging needs the Ollama tile or an API key.

tile.name: Mealie
tile.tagline: Your recipe box — import from any URL.
tile.description: A self-hosted recipe manager and meal planner. Paste a recipe URL and it imports clean.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your account, and paste a recipe URL to import your first recipe.

tile.name: Minecraft Server
tile.tagline: Your own Minecraft world, always on.
tile.description: The canonical homelab game server. Native arm64; instantly understood by non-techies.
tile.postInstall: Point your Minecraft client at <node>.local:25565 to join.

tile.name: Navidrome
tile.tagline: Your own Spotify for the music you own.
tile.description: A fast, lightweight music streaming server that works with a big ecosystem of Subsonic-compatible apps. Featherweight — a perfect always-on tenant for a Pi node.
tile.postInstall: Open it and create your admin account, then point it at your music folder.

tile.name: Ollama + Open WebUI
tile.tagline: Chat with a local LLM your router can't see.
tile.description: Run small language models entirely on your own hardware with a friendly chat UI. A real wow at 1–3B; a disappointment above that on CPU.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your account, then pull a small model (llama3.2:3b) — bigger models crawl on CPU.

tile.name: Paperless-ngx
tile.tagline: Scan, OCR, and search every document.
tile.description: Turn your paper into a searchable archive. Drop a PDF and get full-text OCR search — 'it found my tax form' is a real minor wow.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your admin account, then drop PDFs into the consume folder or upload from the web.

tile.name: Pi-hole
tile.tagline: Network-wide ad blocking — watch the counter climb.
tile.description: Point your network's DNS at Pi-hole and every device gets ad and tracker blocking, with a live dashboard of what it caught. The classic first self-hosted app. Change the admin password before exposing it.
tile.postInstall: The admin password is a placeholder ('changeme') — log in and change it in Settings, then point your devices' DNS at this node.

tiles.compose:

tile.name: RomM
tile.tagline: Your retro game library, playable in the browser.
tile.description: A self-hosted ROM library with box art, metadata, and play-in-browser. Bring your own ROMs.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your account, and point it at your ROMs folder.

tile.name: rtl_433
tile.tagline: Decode your neighborhood's wireless sensors.
tile.description: Sniff 433MHz sensors — weather stations, tire-pressure, thermometers — with a cheap SDR and pipe them to MQTT.
tile.postInstall: Plug in your RTL-SDR; decoded sensor data flows to MQTT and into your dashboards.

tile.name: Shadowbroker
tile.tagline: A global intelligence console on your own metal.
tile.description: An OSINT situational-awareness globe: flights, ships, satellites, quakes, wildfires and more on one MapLibre map. The most on-brand app for Rasputin.
tile.postInstall: Open it and add your OpenSky / AISStream keys in settings for full flight + ship coverage.

tile.name: Trilium Notes
tile.tagline: A personal knowledge base and wiki.
tile.description: A hierarchical note-taking app — great for documenting your homelab. Single container, embedded database.
tile.postInstall: Open it, set your password, and start a note tree.

tile.name: Uptime Kuma
tile.tagline: A self-hosted status board for everything you run.
tile.description: Monitor your services, get an all-green dashboard, and publish a shareable status page. The most-loved monitoring app in the self-hosted community.
tile.postInstall: Open it and create your admin account on the first screen, then add your first monitor.

tiles.compose:
# On 2.x. The raw CVE count is higher than 1.23.17 (1475 vs 176) and that number
# is misleading: v2's OWN dependencies are better (92 fixable in node+go vs 174),
# and the difference is 1383 fixable Debian CVEs from a stale base layer that
# upstream fixes by rebuilding. Different owner, different remediation.
#
# Staying on 1.x was the wrong call for a second reason: 1.23.17 shipped
# 2025-10-20 and is the only 1.x release in twenty months, while 2.x has had
# eight. A branch that no longer gets fixes does not stay at 176.
#
# Still owed: an ACC-1 bench, since this is a major version.
#
# Version is provisional — the ACC-1 bench gate re-pins before ship. The DIGEST is
# what actually fixes the contents: a tag is mutable at the registry however
# specific it looks, so the tag here is human-readable sugar and the digest is the
# pin (ADR-0006 Decision 8).
services:
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.5.0@sha256:a8610b3b4c38077922ba51b036691e06887d7cefd91fe620fd3d6d23d03dc240
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - uptime-kuma-data:/app/data
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"

volumes:
  uptime-kuma-data:

tile.name: Vaultwarden
tile.tagline: Your passwords, on your own metal.
tile.description: A lightweight, self-hosted password manager compatible with the Bitwarden apps and browser extensions.
tile.postInstall: Open it, create your admin account, then install the Bitwarden browser extension and point it here.

tile.name: WeeWX
tile.tagline: Your own weather station dashboard.
tile.description: Publish and archive readings from a real personal weather station. Pairs with an Ecowitt gateway (local LAN) or WeatherFlow Tempest.
tile.postInstall: Point it at your Ecowitt gateway (local LAN) or WeatherFlow Tempest.
